newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to lower with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to lower with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were unchanged to slightly lower Tuesday in thin activity, again undermined by flagging utility demand and further weakness in crude, industry sources said.

"The Gulf feels a bit steadier than New York, but buyers are pretty elusive. There's still no (utility) demand," said one cash trader, noting cheap power and natgas prices also were undercutting fuel oil sentiment.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent held steady at about $15 a barrel, but April one percent paper slipped more than a quarter to $15 or lower on softer crude.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour eased slightly to about $16.75, with cheap power and competitive East Coast city gate gas prices keeping utility fuel requirements to a minimum.

New York city gate swing gas slipped a couple of cents Tuesday to about $2.20/mmBtu, or about a $13.86 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, lost a similar amount to the low-$1.90s/mmBtu, or $12.10 a barrel.
High sulphurs in New York were steady to down slightly.
USG one percent was modestly lower at $13.50-75, while three percent held steady at $12.50.
Traders said there was no word on a Florida utility tender for one percent and 1.8 percent. Bids were due Tuesday.
No NYH or USG deals were confirmed.
